Admission seam (C4): reach listeners. `openReachListener` opens one only while an authenticator provider serves a valid reach policy for it, in a fiber that injects `authenticator`, so it closes before the provider is removed or replaced and never reopens by itself. Its dispatcher removes `tailscale-*` headers, refuses a foreign or loopback `Host`, a foreign SNI, a foreign or absent upgrade `Origin`, the launch token, `/connect` and `dsh-auth-*` cookies, then admits through the provider, sending a pre-login request only to its listed route. `builtinAdmission` exposes Connection's built-in loopback admission for providers to delegate to. The dispatcher also refuses a non-origin-form target (a second `Host` line is answered 400 by the web server before the dispatcher runs), removes identity headers from the parsed, distinct and raw header views, records each admitted connection's session and device for `closeReachConnections`, and applies a policy change announced while the listener binds. Every reach response, refusals included, carries C4's security headers and a Content Security Policy with a fresh nonce, which the pass decision hands to the index renderer; the policy allows no string evaluation, images only from the origin, `data:` and `blob:`, and `no-store` covers `/auth/` and `/api`. The dispatcher records each admitted Peer so Connection can tell reach Peers apart. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges. One-time launch tokens (C4): the dispatcher consumes every one-time launch token a reach request presents before it refuses it. Lead verdict for this change: approved, after an independent review of the change and its fixes (2026-11-10). Lead verdict (2026-11-11): kept; the dispatcher no longer counts Host lines, since the web server refuses a repeated Host line with 400 before the reach gate runs on a reach listener's requests and upgrades; it still refuses a Host other than the rule's, a foreign SNI and an absolute or scheme-relative target.

Admission seam (C4): `admit` returns the dispatcher's Peer for a request a reach listener dispatched and refuses one it admitted as pre-login; a loopback request keeps the Host/Origin fence and then goes to the loaded authenticator provider, or to `builtinAdmission`, upstream's cookie admission unchanged, when none is loaded. `authorizeIndex` answers a reach request by its dispatcher's admission. `ctx.connection` gains `builtinAdmission` and `openReachListener`. A provider's `setCookie` reaches the RPC-channel response, `closeReachConnections` ends the reach connections of a session or device, and with a provider loaded the loopback index is admitted by it and the launch-token exchange at the root and `/connect` runs only while its loopback policy accepts the token. `isReachPeer` reports whether a Peer was admitted on a reach listener. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges. One-time launch tokens (C4): `ctx.connection.oneTimeLaunchTokens` reports the mode, the reach state consumes the tokens a reach request presents, `/connect` and index requests refused by the fence or a provider policy consume theirs, and `consumeStrayLaunchTokens` consumes those of any other loopback request. Admission seam (C4): `openListener` opens additional listeners on the same routes, bound only to an OS-assigned port on `127.0.0.1` or to handed-in byte streams with TLS at the listener, never to a configured host or port. Each listener's gate decides every request and upgrade request before any route, upgrade handler or the fallback: a refusal dispatches nothing, a pass may carry the Peer resources receive, headers pinned through the route's own, and an `only` route outside which the gate's refusal answers. Dispatch moves into `dispatchRequest` and `dispatchUpgrade`, which the configured listener uses without a gate, so its behaviour is unchanged. Every upgrade socket of an additional listener gets its error handler and is tracked before the gate runs, a refused upgrade is destroyed once its refusal is written, and ids are reserved before the bind, so a reset or half-open refused client cannot crash the process or hold close open, and two opens of one id cannot both bind. A pass decision may carry a nonce, which the index renderer receives for that response through an async-local store. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges. One-time launch tokens (C4): the `webserver/request` event is emitted for each request and upgrade request the main listener receives, before routing, so Connection can consume a launch token a request presents outside the exchanges; a listener that throws is logged and the request is routed regardless. Lead verdict for this change: approved, after an independent review of the change and its fixes (2026-11-10). Lead verdict (2026-11-11): kept; every listener answers 400 to a request or upgrade with more than one Host line, counted from the raw headers regardless of case, before any gate, route, upgrade handler or fallback runs.

Protected home, read fence: a read or listing opens the target key and confirms the descriptor is the file or directory the key names before reading through it, so a read tool's protected-read check on the key covers the content when a component of the key is swapped for a link between the check and the open. On Linux the descriptor's `/proc/self/fd` path must equal the key and a listing reads its entries through that descriptor; elsewhere the descriptor's device and inode must equal the key's after the open and the key must still be its own realpath. A mismatch fails with `FS_IO_ERROR`. Reads open with `O_NONBLOCK` outside Windows so a FIFO swapped in after the regular-file check cannot block the open. Mutations: an edit's read and an overwrite's diff basis go through the same confirmed descriptor; every write, create, move and delete holds the target's directory open and confirms it. On Linux missing directories are created through the held parent's descriptor and held without following a link, the staging directory is held without following a link and confirmed private (owner, 0700) and empty, and the temp file, publication and removal are reached through `/proc/self/fd`; elsewhere directories are created by name and confirmed, and the staging directory and the published file are confirmed by path (removing a misplaced publication). A changed path fails with `FS_IO_ERROR`. The staging directory is removed without walking it (unlink the temp file, then a non-recursive `rmdir` that leaves a non-empty directory or a link in its name in place), and a misplaced one outside Linux only when empty. A listing leaves out a child link that resolves through itself (`ELOOP`) instead of failing. Content, errors and limits are otherwise upstream's. Lead verdict (2026-11-11): kept; on Linux every write, create, move, edit and delete reaches the target directory, the directories it creates and the staging directory through held descriptors opened without following links, and the staging directory is removed without recursion, so a link swapped in after the checks fails the mutation with FS_IO_ERROR; outside Linux the path checks are best effort as documented.
